title: Trace ownership through a live shard move
description: Select a migration state to see the active read, copy, catch-up, verification, and cutover paths. The ownership epoch prevents stale components from accepting writes at the wrong owner.

nodes.label: Application
nodes.detail: Sends the logical partition key and a request ID. A retried write keeps the same idempotency identity while ownership changes.

nodes.label: Shard router
nodes.detail: Resolves a logical bucket to one physical owner. It refreshes stale entries after an epoch rejection or moved response.

nodes.label: Ownership directory
nodes.detail: Stores the current owner and monotonically increasing epoch for each logical shard. Cutover changes this record atomically.

nodes.label: Source shard
nodes.detail: Serves reads and writes until cutover. During migration it exposes a consistent snapshot and an ordered stream of later changes, including deletes.

nodes.label: Migration worker
nodes.detail: Copies bounded batches from a snapshot, persists progress, and retries idempotently without changing the authoritative owner.

nodes.label: Target shard
nodes.detail: Receives backfill and ordered changes but does not accept authoritative traffic until verification passes and the directory advances the epoch.

nodes.label: Verifier
nodes.detail: Compares row counts, checksums, sampled records, tombstones, and change-stream lag before approving cutover or rollback.

nodes.label: Migration audit
nodes.detail: Records checkpoints, verification results, epoch changes, stale-route rejections, rollback decisions, and final source deletion.

scenarios.label: Steady state
scenarios.summary: The directory identifies the source as owner at epoch 41. Requests follow one route, and the target is not yet authoritative.
scenarios.result: The source is the only writer for this logical shard. Every on-call tool should be able to resolve the same owner and epoch from the shard key.

scenarios.label: Copy + catch up
scenarios.summary: User traffic still reaches the source while a checkpointed snapshot copy and ordered change stream bring the target up to date.
scenarios.result: The source remains authoritative. The target may be incomplete, so a worker restart resumes from a durable checkpoint instead of changing routing.

scenarios.label: Verified cutover
scenarios.summary: Backfill is complete, change lag is inside the cutover bound, and verification matches. The old owner is fenced before the directory advances to epoch 42.
scenarios.result: New requests reach the target at epoch 42. The source stays read-only during a rollback window and rejects writes carrying the new epoch.

scenarios.label: Source fails mid-copy
scenarios.summary: The source becomes unavailable before the candidate has caught up and verification has passed. Some copied rows exist, but ownership has not changed.
scenarios.result: Do not promote the partial target. Recover the source shard or one of its replicas, keep epoch 41 authoritative, then resume from the last durable checkpoint.

scenarios.label: Stale router
scenarios.summary: The directory and target are at epoch 42, but one router still sends a request to the source using cached epoch 41 ownership.
scenarios.result: The fenced source rejects the stale route or returns a moved response. The router refreshes epoch 42 and retries with the same request ID instead of creating split-brain writes.
